title: Decor that looks planned, and a safe start

say: Decor that looks planned, and a safe start.
This is the video for module one of Event Decoration and Styling.
A decorator turns a church hall, a canopy or a living room into a setting for one occasion. The client is paying for four things. First, a look that suits the event.

Start with small jobs, like a home birthday, where a mistake can be fixed in twenty minutes.

say: Decor that looks expensive is rarely about money. It is about colour control. A hall with three colours repeated everywhere looks planned. Seven colours look confused.
Monochrome is one colour in light, medium and dark shades, plus white.

cards.d: One colour in light, medium and dark, plus white. Blush, rose and deep pink for a girl's birthday.
Two or three colours side by side on the wheel. Gold, orange and burnt orange for a traditional wedding.
Two colours opposite on the wheel, one dominant. Royal blue with gold accents for a thanksgiving.

say: Analogous is two or three colours sitting next to each other on the colour wheel, like gold, orange and burnt orange.

cards.d: One colour in light, medium and dark, plus white. Blush, rose and deep pink for a girl's birthday.

say: Complementary is two colours opposite each other, with one dominant, like royal blue with gold accents. Gold and silver behave like neutrals and suit most schemes.

say: Use the 60-30-10 rule. About 60 percent is the main colour, 30 percent a second colour, and 10 percent an accent.
For example, Funke is decorating a 50th birthday in Ibadan. The celebrant wants classy and green, and her aso ebi is emerald lace. Funke asks for a photo of the actual fabric.

items: 60% ivory: tablecloths and chair covers
30% emerald: runners and balloon clusters
10% gold: chargers, candle holders, the 50
Focal point: backdrop behind her chair

panel.rule: One clear focal point. Spend most of your effort there.

say: Decoration fails less from poor taste, and more from practical gaps. Ask yourself four questions.

panel.heading: Four questions before you say yes
items: Skills: garlands, tables, draping
Transport: how will items reach the venue?
People: one or two reliable helpers
Time: early setup, stay to pack down

say: For example, Halima in Kaduna is asked to decorate a church reception for 150 guests. She has never dressed 15 round tables, so she practises one at home and times herself: 12 minutes.

panel.heading: Halima's check before saying yes
items: Practise one table: 12 minutes
15 tables: about 90 minutes with a helper
Book rental delivery for tables
Real candles near dried flowers? Go flameless

panel.rule: Find the gaps before the day, not on the day.

say: Learn these rules now. Keep candles at least 12 inches, about 30 cm, from anything that can burn. Near drapes, flowers or balloons, use flameless candles. Never plug one extension box into another.

panel.heading: Safety before guests arrive
items: Candles 12 inches from fabric, or flameless
No extension box plugged into another
Cables taped flat, away from water
Generators outside only
Ladder held by a helper
Heavy pieces weighted or tied

say: Tape cables flat, away from drinks and water. Generators make carbon monoxide, a poisonous gas you cannot smell. They must run outside, never inside a hall or canopy.

panel.heading: Safety before guests arrive

say: Use a proper step ladder, never a stacked chair, with a helper holding it. Weight backdrop stands and arches, and tie them down outdoors.
Light fabrics like chiffon burn fast. And find the fire extinguisher and the exits before you start.

say: To remember. Clients pay for a look, reliability, safety and peace of mind. Use about three colours, in 60-30-10, with one focal point. Close your practical gaps before you say yes. And keep candles away from fabric and generators outside.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Clients pay for look, reliability, safety, peace

60-30-10, and one clear focal point
Check gaps: skills, transport, people, time
Candles away from fabric; generators outside
